title.narrative: Integrated Multi-Sectoral Life-Saving Response for IDPs and host communities in Adigrat, Eastern Zone of Tigray Region

description.narrative: ltpgtThe humanitarian crisis in Northern Ethiopia remains one of the most severe in the world, driven by the devastating legacy of conflict, climate shocks, and mass displacement. According to the IOM Displacement Tracking Matrix (March 2025), the situation remains fluid, with Northern Ethiopia still hosting a significant proportion of the country's 3.5 million Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs). The Eastern Zone of Tigray, and specifically Adigrat town, epitomizes this protracted emergency. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtThe erosion of essential public services has created alarming humanitarian conditions. Access to primary healthcare is extremely limited, and the breakdown of water and sanitation systems has triggered the spread of waterborne diseases. Protection risks have sharply escalated, with increasing cases of family separation, gender-based violence (GBV), and child exploitation. Malnutrition among children and pregnant and lactating women (PLWs) remains above emergency thresholds, while psychosocial distress continues to affect both displaced and host populations.ltbrgtIn response, this project—submitted under the Ethiopia Humanitarian Fund (EHF) Third Reserve Allocation—proposes a comprehensive, integrated life-saving intervention targeting 102,598 of the most vulnerable IDPs and host community members in Adigrat. The overall objective is to reduce excess morbidity and mortality while strengthening protection systems and resilience through a coordinated, multi-sectoral response.ltbrgtHealth: Two Mobile Health and Nutrition Teams (MHNTs) will provide essential Primary Health Care (PHC), Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS), and Sexual and Reproductive Health and Rights (SRHR) services. The project will rehabilitate two damaged health facilities to restore static service delivery and strengthen community-based disease surveillance to prevent outbreaks.ltbrgtNutrition: The intervention will conduct systematic screening of 550 children under five and PLWs for acute malnutrition, provide life-saving treatment for 170 cases of Severe and Moderate Acute Malnutrition (SAM/MAM), and establish 50 Mother-to-Mother Support Groups to promote Infant and Young Child Feeding (IYCF) practices, contributing to sustainable nutrition outcomes.ltbrgtWASH: To address the acute shortage of safe water, the project will provide immediate water trucking to 2,667 beneficiaries, procure a 10,000-liter tanker for sustainable supply, and rehabilitate six gender-segregated latrine blocks to ensure dignified and safe sanitation facilities.ltbrgtChild Protection and GBV: The project will deliver gender- and age-sensitive case management to 270 at-risk children, facilitate Family Tracing and Reunification (FTR) for 100 unaccompanied and separated children, and establish three Safe Spaces to provide structured psychosocial support. In addition, local community structures will be trained to identify, refer, and mitigate protection and GBV risks.ltbrgtMulti-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA): Cash interventions will be integrated across sectors to empower vulnerable households. Conditional cash transfers will support 100 alternative caregivers in foster arrangements, while unconditional multipurpose cash will help families meet their basic needs, reduce negative coping mechanisms, and reinforce the effectiveness of other life-saving interventions.ltbrgtThis holistic and integrated response was developed in close coordination with sub-national clusters, relevant line bureaus, and local authorities to ensure alignment with cluster priorities, efficiency in delivery, and the avoidance of duplication. The project adheres to core humanitarian principles and mainstreams cross-cutting commitments to Protection, Gender Equality, Disability Inclusion, and Accountability to Affected Populations (AAP) throughout the implementation cycle.lt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
